record.context_brief: primordial origin of massive gravitational-wave black holes
record.original_question: For axion-like particle models in which closed domain walls collapse into primordial black holes over the mass interval M_min = f(m_Pl/Λ)^2 to M_max = f(m_Pl/f)^2(m_Pl/Λ)^2, can the black holes with masses above 50 solar masses observed through LIGO/VIRGO gravitational-wave coalescences have a primordial origin in this ALP domain-wall mechanism?

evidence.quote: The interval of mass M of domain walls, collapsing in primordial black holes (PBH) [16, 29], is given by Mmin = f (mPl / Λ)^2 ≤ M ≤ Mmax = f (mPl / f)^2 (mPl / Λ)^2.

At the appropriate value of f and Λ the ALP mechanisms can provide formation of PBHs with stellar mass, and even larger, up to the values corresponding to the seeds for Super Massive Black Holes in Active Galactic nuclei (AGN) [30, 31, 32]. Their mass can easily exceed the limit of pair instability and the LIGO/VIRGO detected gravitational wave signal from coalescence of black holes with masses M > 50M⊙ naturally puts forward the question on their primordial origin [33, 34].

artifact.category_tag: primordial black holes from axion-like particle domain walls
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an axion-like particle (ALP) model characterized by two energy scales: a symmetry-breaking scale $f$ and an explicit-symmetry-breaking (instanton) scale $\Lambda$, with $\Lambda \ll f \ll m_{\mathrm{Pl}}$, where $m_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ denotes the Planck mass. In such a model, closed domain walls produced after the two-stage breaking of the $U(1)$ symmetry can collapse and form primordial black holes (PBHs). Assume that the resulting PBH mass spectrum spans the interval
$$M_{\min} = f\left(\frac{m_{\mathrm{Pl}}}{\Lambda}\right)^{2} \;\le\; M \;\le\; M_{\max} = f\left(\frac{m_{\mathrm{Pl}}}{f}\right)^{2}\left(\frac{m_{\mathrm{Pl}}}{\Lambda}\right)^{2}.$$

Gravitational-wave observatories (such as LIGO/Virgo) have detected coalescences of black holes with individual masses exceeding $50\, M_{\odot}$, lying within or beyond the pair-instability mass gap predicted for stellar-collapse origin.

Question: Do there exist physically admissible values of the parameters $f$ and $\Lambda$ (consistent with cosmological and astrophysical constraints) such that the above ALP domain-wall collapse mechanism produces a population of PBHs whose mass distribution includes black holes with $M > 50\, M_{\odot}$ in sufficient abundance to account for the observed gravitational-wave merger events? Equivalently, can the black holes with $M > 50\, M_{\odot}$ inferred from observed gravitational-wave coalescences have a primordial origin via this ALP domain-wall mechanism?
artifact.status_search_result: The primordial origin of LIGO/Virgo black holes above the pair-instability gap (M > 50 M_sun) remains an actively debated open question, with multiple proposed formation channels (including ALP domain-wall collapse) under investigation but none confirmed. No definitive resolution has been established as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Open questions of BSM Cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: the LIGO/VIRGO detected gravitational wave signal from coalescence of black holes with masses M > 50 M⊙ naturally puts forward the question on their primordial origin
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether such heavy LIGO/Virgo black holes are primordial is posed as open.
